messages.author: b647a89a4db2f284
messages.subject: Re: Factor scores from blavInspect()
parts:
Hi!

In relation to this question about the relationship between applying lavPredict() and blavInspect() to a blavaan object, I was wondering whether the high correlations among the latent factor scores is also taken to be an indicator that the estimated factor scores by lavPredict() can be used for a blavaan object.

The reason I am asking is that unlike BlavPredict(), lavPredict() returns the labels of the latent factor scores, and so if multiple latent factors are estimated across multiple groups, then the data structure without the labels is a bit difficult to handle without a map of which order the latent factor scores are entered.

To compare: with two latent factors across two groups (where the groups correspond to a within-participant manipulation) and 769 participants, lavPredict() returns a list of 2 separated with labels across the two groups with a labelled column for each factor score with 769 rows. In contrast, BlavPredict() returns a list of 2 without labels with 16000 rows (for the different draws of the posterior distribution) with 3076 columns that are labelled "eta[1:1538, 1:2]".

I would assume that "eta[1:769, 1]" corresponds to the factor scores of the first latent factor in the first group, that "eta[1:769, 2]" corresponds to the second latent factor in the first group, that "eta[770:1538, 1]" corresponds to the first latent factor in the second group, and that "eta[770:1538, 2]" corresponds to the second latent factor in the second group. But without the labels of the factors and the groups (which here correspond to a within-participant manipulation), I would feel less confident assuming that this is the correct interpretation. And so, if I could just as well use the labelled factor scores returned by applying lavPredict() to the blavaan object, I would be more confident about which scores correspond to what.

Thanks in advance!

Best ,
Niels

messages.subject: Re: Factor scores from blavInspect()
parts:
Niels,

I recently fixed a factor score labeling issue, see here:

https://github.com/ecmerkle/blavaan/issues/53

This fix currently is on the github version of blavaan, but not yet the CRAN version.

But I also wonder whether you are using JAGS instead of Stan. I cannot guarantee that the fixes address target="jags". If you are using JAGS, I will have to look.

Best,
Ed

parts:
Ed,

thanks, this is helpful!

Since I did not overwrite the default of bsem(), and str() of the model object includes 'stan_args', I assume it is stan.

I will try updating with the github version and see whether it helps.

From the github-issue you linked to, I can see that I probably need to use blavInspect(model, "lvmeans") for my purposes, anyway.

Trying that I can see (prior to updating blavaan) that the posterior means of the latent factors are labelled with the parameter names in columns, but that the posterior means of the different groups are concatenated (instead of being separated with labels as in lavPredict()). Possibly, you fixed this as well with the update (I will check), but I guess the order of the groups should be fixed and the same as in lavaan, so here I would be able to sort out the concatenated posterior means even without the labels.

Best,
Niels
